name: ClinuxFlowProvider
title: ClinuxFlow Provider (the person)
description: A healthcare professional's own identity, profiling FHIR R4 Practitioner. Grounded directly against the real Healthcare Professional Registry (HPR) Create-HPRID API (docs/NHPR SBX Doc/NHPR Doc/HPR/1. Register Healthcare Professional (Doctor & Nurse) API.pdf, its own Mandatory-field table) — not the prior YAML, which conflated the person (Practitioner) with their role at one facility (see ClinuxFlowProviderRole, a separate profile) by piling both onto Practitioner.extension.

element.comment: HPR createHprId: firstName (Required) + middleName (optional) — modeled as HumanName.given[0]/given[1], the standard FHIR home for a given/middle name, not a single freetext name.
HPR: lastName, optional (a real HPR quirk — the person-level API allows no surname; a workplace-role display name is a separate, ProviderRole-level concern).
HPR: gender ('M'/'F'/...), captured on the real /checkHpIdAccountExist response — bound to FHIR's own administrative-gender ValueSet, not a re-encoded HPR string.

HPR returns yearOfBirth/monthOfBirth/dayOfBirth as three separate fields (Aadhaar-sourced) — composed into one real FHIR date here, the standard element for it, rather than three separate custom fields.
HPR: profilePhoto, optional base64 image.
HPR createHprId: email, Required.
HPR: mobile, captured during Aadhaar/OTP verification, not the createHprId payload itself.

HPR createHprId: hprId (Required, from the Get-Suggestion API — e.g. 'userid@hpr.abdm'), and the real HPR-issued hprIdNumber returned once created. This is the one genuine business identifier every provider profile needs; license/registration numbers (real, distinct identifiers) are separate slices below.

The professional's real state/council medical registration/license number — genuinely a business identifier (Practitioner.qualification also exists for the qualification itself; this slice is the registration number, which qualification.identifier could also carry, but a top-level identifier slice keeps it consistent with hprId's own shape and easy to query).
HPR: sourceType (e.g. 'AADHAAR') — how this identity was originally verified. No standard FHIR element for identity-verification provenance at this level; a real extension.
HPR createHprId: hpCategoryCode, Required — real HPR code table: 1=Doctor, 2=Nurse. Bound to that real 2-value ValueSet, not an open string.

HPR: hpSubCategoryCode, Required — real HPR code table, e.g. 1=Modern Medicine, 2=Dentist, 3=Ayurveda, 4=Unani, 89=Sowa-Rigpa, 5=Siddha, 6=Homoeopathy (doctor); 7=RANM, 9=RN & RM, 10=RLHV, 8=RN (nurse). Bound to that real, cited table — not this app's own invented specialty list.
HPR: council, a real boolean (Optional).
HPR: stateCode (LGD state code from master data), Optional — the state this professional's registration is anchored to; distinct from any one facility's own address.
HPR: districtCode, Optional.

register-professional-new: personalInformation.salutation, Optional — no standard FHIR element for a title/salutation at this level (HumanName.prefix exists but this app's own Practitioner.name is a single .text/.given/.family, not prefix-bearing), a real extension.
register-professional-new: personalInformation.nationality, Optional.
register-professional-new: personalInformation.fatherName, Optional.
register-professional-new: personalInformation.motherName, Optional.
register-professional-new: personalInformation.spouseName, Optional.

register-professional-new: personalInformation.languagesKnown, Optional — stored as one comma-separated extension value rather than Communication.language (that binds to a coded ValueSet this app has no matching master data for; a real, if simplified, home).

register-professional-new: currentWorkDetails.currentlyWorking, Optional — no standard FHIR element for this on Practitioner itself (PractitionerRole.active covers active-at-a-specific-role, not a person-level employment declaration).

register-professional-new: currentWorkDetails.purposeOfRegistration, Optional. NHPR user manual's own "Nature of Work" step explicitly allows selecting more than one (Practice/Administrative/Teaching/Teleconsultation) — widened from max:1 to max:* to match; abdmAdapter.js's buildPractitionerPayload joins the selections back into one string for the real API, whose own true singular/array shape isn't independently confirmed (same honest-gap treatment already applied elsewhere in this profile).
NHPR user manual's own Work Details step — a real field shown right next to Nature of Work, relevant when Teleconsultation is one of the selected options. No confirmed live API field name.
register-professional-new: currentWorkDetails.chooseWorkStatus, Optional.

register-professional-new: currentWorkDetails.reasonForNotWorking — mandatory only when currentlyWorking is false, per the real spec's own note; enforced in the UI, not here (no conditional-required primitive in this validator yet).
register-professional-new: currentWorkDetails.facilityId — the real ABDM Facility ID, once picked via ProviderWorkExperienceHost.vue's own Search Facility panel.
register-professional-new: currentWorkDetails.facilityDeclarationData.facilityName — mandatory only when facilityId isn't already known, per the real spec's own note; enforced in the UI.
register-professional-new: currentWorkDetails.facilityDeclarationData.facilityAddress, Optional.
register-professional-new: currentWorkDetails.facilityDeclarationData.pincode, Optional.
register-professional-new: currentWorkDetails.facilityDeclarationData.facilityType, Optional.
register-professional-new: currentWorkDetails.facilityDeclarationData.department, Optional.
register-professional-new: currentWorkDetails.facilityDeclarationData.designation, Optional.

register-professional-new: currentWorkDetails.facilityDeclarationData.ministry — mandatory only when chooseWorkStatus is Government or Both, per the real spec's own note; enforced in the UI. No getAllMinistry master data exists yet.

NHPR user manual's own Work Details step: Central/State radio shown when Work Status is Government or Both, gating whether a Ministry (Central) or a state government department is being declared. No confirmed live API field name — same honest-gap treatment as :workMinistry above.
NHPR user manual's own Work Details step: "Are you working in a PSU?" — only shown when workGovtCategory is Central.
NHPR user manual's own Work Details step — free text, no getAllPSU master data exists anywhere (same honest-gap treatment as :workMinistry).

NHPR user manual's own Work Details step — a base64 attachment (appointment letter/pay-slip/transfer order) the manual marks MANDATORY whenever Work Status is Government or Both; enforced in the UI, not here (no conditional-required primitive in this validator yet).

NHPR user manual, Preview Profile step ("About" text shown alongside public display settings before e-sign) — no real ABDM API field confirmed for this yet (no register/update-professional spec block documents it); captured locally as an honest gap, same discipline facilityTypeCode/facilitySubtype etc. already carry, in case a future spec revision adds it.
NHPR user manual, Preview Profile step's own "Anyone assisted you to register in HPR?" Yes/No question — same honest-gap treatment as :about above, no confirmed live API field.

ClinuxFlow-local tracking flag, not an ABDM field — set once register-professional-new succeeds, so ProviderHprPanel.vue's own RegistrationLedger reloads onto the correct Attestation/Submitted stage instead of resetting to Preview (same role hospital_additional_info_submitted/hospital_detailed_info_submitted already play for FacilityHfrPanel.vue).

NHPR user manual's own Preview Profile step ("Your profile will be visible to the public, choose public display settings") — mirrors hospital_public_display_optout's existing role for Organization/HFR; staff_public_mobile/staff_landline/staff_public_email stay the always-captured fields this just gates visibility of, same relationship FacilityHfrPanel.vue's own publicDisplay reactive already has to Organization's public contact fields.

register-professional-new: registrationAcademic.registrationData[] — a real, repeating base FHIR BackboneElement, the correct home (not an extension). Deliberately declared as a PLAIN element here, not sliced on its own nested .extension (unlike Practitioner.extension/.telecom/.identifier above) — this validator's own generic slice-cardinality check flattens a sliced array ACROSS every repetition of an enclosing repeating element (confirmed by reading resolvePath/groupElements together: resolvePath walks straight through Practitioner.qualification's own 0..* before reaching .extension, so a max:1 per-field slice check would incorrectly count e.g. 2 different qualifications' 2 separate 'country' extensions as one array of 2, failing a max:1 constraint that is actually satisfied within each qualification). Scoping slice cardinality per-repetition-of-an-array is real, separate validator work, not attempted here — ProviderQualificationsHost.vue's own YAML-side FHIR_ARRAY_PATHS entry for 'Practitioner.qualification.extension' is what keeps each qualification's own extensions correctly scoped at the DATA layer; this profile just leaves qualification.extension's own children as open/unsliced (the StructureDefinition default) rather than risk a false-positive conformance failure on exactly the multi-qualification case this app's own onboarding was built and tested against.

register-professional-new: registrationAcademic.registrationData[].qualification (the degree/diploma code) — the real spec's own required field per qualification entry. max is deliberately '*', not '1': this element's own path descends through Practitioner.qualification's 0..* repetition, and this validator's checkCardinality counts the FLATTENED total across every qualification (same resolvePath behavior documented on the Practitioner.qualification element just above) — a practitioner with 2 qualifications correctly produces 2 .code values total, which a max:1 here would have wrongly rejected (confirmed by reasoning through the exact multi-qualification case this app's own onboarding was tested against). min:1 still correctly means 'at least one qualification has a code' in aggregate.
